primary_topics: Keynote address at the Third Philippine Conference on New Evangelization (PCNE), July 16, 2016 -- invited by Cardinal Tagle to speak on 'On the Basis of Love: Malasakit sa Bayan ni Juan de la Cruz' under the theme AWA, UNAWA, GAWA

CJP's journey of faith: from near-death at age six (dysentery, no medical care, miraculous recovery) through Catholic ignorance (UST Trinity failure) to the Pontifical Council for the Laity at the Vatican (1996-2001)

CJP's journey of reason: from impoverished newsboy to Manila Times dream fulfilled (Inquirer President 1991); from failed Yale travel grant to Salonga's law office apprenticeship; from bar exams while ill to 6th place
Policy applications of faith and reason: vigilance on the proposed federal system and the death penalty proposal -- the latter clearly violating the Ten Commandments and the sacredness of life
sub_topics: CJP's hesitation at nearly 80 years old to accept the PCNE invitation; struck by the concept paper's words: 'we are basically a people soaked in the values of the Gospel... we have been mercified'
Two basic truths proclaimed: (1) God's mercy and love felt through Catholic faith; (2) God's wisdom experienced through the gift of reason
World War II dysentery miracle: at age six in Candaba, Pampanga, afflicted with dysentery; no hospital, doctor or nurse; given up for dead; miraculous recovery without medical attention

Newsboy dream: hawking newspapers in Sampaloc, Manila; promised himself he would be president of the Manila Times (then the largest-circulated newspaper); by God's mercy, became President of the Philippine Daily Inquirer in 1991

UST Trinity failure: applied for scholarship; Dominican priest asked three questions; for 'Name them' (the three persons of the Holy Trinity) CJP whispered 'Jesus, Mary, Joseph'; denied scholarship; went to FEU instead

FEU as God's blessing: met Dr. Alejandro R. Roces (adviser in student leadership), Law Dean Jovito R. Salonga (life-long mentor), and Fr. Michael Nolan (FEU Chaplain; recruited into Student Catholic Action)
Meeting Leni: in the National Union of Students (NUS), met Leni Carpio who represented St. Scholastica's College; 'She wanted to be a Benedictine nun, until she met me. She taught me how to pray.'

Growing in faith: Marriage Encounter and Life in the Spirit Seminars; charismatic Catholic; read Bible several times and over 100 religious books; lay delegate to Second Plenary Council of the Philippines (1991); Pope John Paul II named him only Filipino in the Pontifical Council of the Laity (Vatican, 1996-2001)

Journey of reason: shy teenager wanting to be a chemical engineer; strong-willed father directed him to law (his own frustrated ambition); father died when CJP was a first-year pre-law student; vowed at deathbed to fulfill father's ambition
Bar exams 1960: got sick; hospitalized; had to wade through knee-deep floodwater to the exam venue; wanted to quit after lackluster first day; Salonga would not hear of it; placed 6th

Yale scholarship denied: granted scholarship but could not secure travel grant from US Embassy; Salonga consoled: 'Forget graduate studies. Come and join my law office and I will teach you what I learned from UP, Harvard and Yale'

Policy vigilance: most crucial temporal governance matter is President Duterte's proposal to institute the federal system; death penalty proposal 'clearly violates the Ten Commandments, as well as the sacredness of life and the dignity of the human person enshrined in our Bible and in our Constitution'

Closing doxology: 'our God will never abandon us. He will always be with us: above us to inspire us, behind us to strengthen us, before us to lead us, and within us to transform us to be another Christ. To God be the glory! Alleluia!'

stances.claim: The death penalty proposal 'clearly violates the Ten Commandments, as well as the sacredness of life and the dignity of the human person enshrined in our Bible and in our Constitution.' This is CJP's most direct and unambiguous policy position on a Duterte-era proposal -- unusually categorical, delivered before a Catholic evangelization conference.
stances.rhetorical_move: faith-and-law convergence: the death penalty is condemned on both theological (Ten Commandments) and constitutional (human dignity) grounds simultaneously
stances.confidence: asserted with categorical certainty, unusually direct for CJP's normally measured political register

stances.claim: The malasakit (care and concern) that Cardinal Tagle's PCNE theme calls for must be grounded in both faith and reason -- not just awa (mercy) as sentiment but as an actionable civic culture embedded in governance and public service. CJP's personal testimony is offered as proof that faith and reason are not in tension but mutually reinforcing.
stances.rhetorical_move: faith-reason synthesis as personal testimony: CJP's life story as the experiential proof that both are needed and compatible

stances.claim: Every apparent setback in CJP's life -- the dysentery, the UST rejection, the Yale travel grant denial, the bar illness -- was redirected by God's mercy into a greater opportunity. 'It was not because of, but in spite of' the obstacles that CJP became who he is.
stances.rhetorical_move: providential-reversal pattern: each failure named and reframed as a divine redirection toward a better outcome

notable_anecdotes: The dysentery miracle: at age six in wartime Candaba, Pampanga, CJP was afflicted with dysentery with no hospital, doctor or nurse available. He was given up for dead but miraculously recovered without medical attention -- his first experience of God's mercy.

Newsboy dream fulfilled: hawking newspapers in Sampaloc and promising himself he would be president of the Manila Times. By God's mercy, became President of the Philippine Daily Inquirer instead in 1991 -- 'the largest-circulated daily currently.'

The UST Trinity failure (PCNE version): for the question 'Name the three persons of the Holy Trinity,' CJP 'sheepishly whispered, Jesus, Mary, Joseph' and was denied the UST scholarship. Going to FEU instead turned out to be one of the best turns of his life.
Leni Carpio's vocation: 'She wanted to be a Benedictine nun, until she met me. She taught me how to pray.' -- CJP's most compact summary of their meeting and its spiritual significance.

Salonga's consolation for the Yale denial: 'Forget graduate studies. Come and join my law office and I will teach you what I learned from UP, Harvard and Yale.' And teach me, he grandly did -- three years of apprenticeship before CJP set up his own law firm.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered July 16, 2016 at the Third Philippine Conference on New Evangelization (PCNE) at Cardinal Tagle's invitation -- the theme being AWA, UNAWA, GAWA and 'Malasakit sa Bayan ni Juan de la Cruz' -- this keynote by CJP (nearly 80 years old, initially hesitant) proclaims two basic truths: God's mercy felt through Catholic faith, and God's wisdom experienced through the gift of reason. The journey of faith begins with a World War II dysentery miracle at age six in Candaba, Pampanga (given up for dead; no medical care; miraculous recovery); continues through the newsboy years in Sampaloc (promising himself he would be president of the Manila Times, fulfilled in 1991 as Inquirer President); through the UST Trinity failure ('sheepishly whispered, Jesus, Mary, Joseph'; denied scholarship; went to FEU instead -- one of the best turns of his life); through meeting Fr. Michael Nolan at FEU (Student Catholic Action), then Leni Carpio at the NUS ('She wanted to be a Benedictine nun, until she met me. She taught me how to pray'); through Marriage Encounter, Life in the Spirit, reading the Bible several times and 100+ religious books, the 1991 Second Plenary Council, and ultimately Pope John Paul II's appointment as the only Filipino in the Pontifical Council of the Laity (Vatican, 1996-2001). The journey of reason parallels it: father's deathbed vow (to fulfill his frustrated law ambition); bar exams while sick, wading through knee-deep flood, wanted to quit, Salonga insisted, placed 6th; Yale scholarship granted but travel grant denied; Salonga's consolation: 'Forget graduate studies. Come and join my law office and I will teach you what I learned from UP, Harvard and Yale.' Policy applications: vigilance on the federal system proposal; the death penalty proposal 'clearly violates the Ten Commandments, as well as the sacredness of life and the dignity of the human person.' Closes: 'God will always be with us: above us to inspire us, behind us to strengthen us, before us to lead us, and within us to transform us to be another Christ. To God be the glory! Alleluia!'
